evidence.claim: A linkage attack using published turn order, timing, token counts, and style against fully anonymized 8-seat x 12-round sessions reports mean accuracy at chance (1/8), with chance baseline computed not assumed.
Field census of the published artifact finds zero real participant ids or display names.

mechanisms: keyed Fisher-Yates shuffle of turn order
strip timing, token counts, and stylometric text

manifest_registration.note: per-unit only; did not run unit_manifest.py --write

negative_controls.description: Keep names masked and strip timing/tokens/style, but do not shuffle seating order. Order-channel linkage must rise above chance.

notes: G-1 IMP-0276: live named probes exit 0, honest SUCCESS receipt, per-unit manifest row. cloud ok=true is not delivery.

residual_unknowns.claim: IMP-0264 council kernel is not on this worktree, so this module is a standalone transform. A kernel that writes turns without calling publish_session would bypass it.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Wire publish_session into tools/council/kernel.py event loop when IMP-0264 exists and re-run the linkage battery on kernel-emitted transcripts.

residual_unknowns.claim: Vote/position payload uniqueness can still cluster seats when a stance is rare. The contracted attack channels are order, timing, token counts, and style.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Add optional stance-bucketing if a future protocol requires unlinkable payloads as well as unlinkable labels.
